characters.name: Moses
characters.note: Israelite leader and lawgiver, raised in Pharaoh's house; deliverer of Israel from Egypt (Exodus).

characters.name: Aaron
characters.note: Brother of Moses, spokesman and first high priest (Exodus).

characters.name: Pharaoh
aliases: the new king who didn't know Joseph
characters.note: King of Egypt who oppresses Israel and refuses to release them; unnamed in Exodus.

characters.name: Pharaoh's daughter
characters.note: Daughter of Pharaoh who finds and adopts the infant Moses (Exodus).

characters.name: Miriam
characters.note: Sister of Moses and Aaron; watches over baby Moses and leads the women's song at the sea (Exodus).

characters.name: Zipporah
characters.note: Midianite wife of Moses (Exodus).

characters.name: Jethro
characters.note: Priest of Midian, father-in-law of Moses; advises him on judging (Exodus).

characters.name: Joshua
characters.note: Moses' servant and military commander against Amalek (Exodus).

characters.name: Shiphrah
characters.note: Hebrew midwife who defies Pharaoh's order to kill baby boys (Exodus).

characters.name: Puah
characters.note: Hebrew midwife who defies Pharaoh's order to kill baby boys (Exodus).

characters.name: Israel
characters.note: The Israelite people as a body; acts as a group in many scenes (Exodus).

characters.name: the Egyptians
characters.note: The Egyptian people and army; act as a group in the pursuit at the sea (Exodus).

characters.name: the magicians
characters.note: Egyptian magicians who imitate some of Moses' signs (Exodus).

characters.name: Amalek
characters.note: Enemy people who attack Israel at Rephidim (Exodus).

characters.name: Bezalel
characters.note: Craftsman filled with God's Spirit to build the tabernacle (Exodus).

characters.name: Oholiab
characters.note: Craftsman who assists Bezalel in building the tabernacle (Exodus).

characters.name: Nadab and Abihu
characters.note: Sons of Aaron; present at the mountain meal in Exodus 24.

characters.name: the elders of Israel
characters.note: Israelite elders who act as a body in several scenes (Exodus); the elders who ask for a king in 1 Samuel are a separate group.

characters.name: God
characters.note: The deity; appears as voice, fire, cloud and angel; never depicted as a human figure.

characters.name: Hur
characters.note: Companion of Moses who helps hold up his hands in the battle with Amalek (Exodus).

characters.name: Joseph
characters.note: Son of Jacob, dead in Egypt; his bones are carried out by Moses (Exodus).

characters.name: the serpent
aliases: the rod turned to a snake
characters.note: Aaron's rod made serpent; an object rather than a separate character (Exodus).

characters.name: Elkanah
characters.note: Ephraimite husband of Hannah and Peninnah, father of Samuel (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Hannah
characters.note: Wife of Elkanah, mother of Samuel (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Peninnah
characters.note: Other wife of Elkanah (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Eli
characters.note: Old priest at Shiloh, judge of Israel (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Hophni
characters.note: Wicked son of Eli, priest (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Phinehas
characters.note: Wicked son of Eli, priest; not to be confused with the Phinehas of Numbers (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Samuel
characters.note: Prophet and judge, son of Hannah (1 Samuel).

characters.name: a man of God
characters.note: Unnamed prophet who rebukes Eli (1 Samuel 2:27).

characters.name: Phinehas' wife
characters.note: Wife of Phinehas, mother of Ichabod; unnamed (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Ichabod
characters.note: Newborn son named by his mother; named only at birth (1 Samuel).

characters.name: the people of Ashdod
characters.note: Philistine townsfolk who move the ark (1 Samuel).

characters.name: the lords of the Philistines
characters.note: Philistine rulers who consult on the ark (1 Samuel).

characters.name: the men of Beth Shemesh
characters.note: Israelites who look into the ark (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Abinadab
characters.note: Man of Kiriath Jearim who keeps the ark (1 Samuel); distinct from Abinadab son of Jesse, a brother of David.

characters.name: the people of Israel
characters.note: Israelite people as a collective voice (1 Samuel); the same people as in Exodus.

characters.name: Saul
characters.note: First king of Israel, son of Kish (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Kish
characters.note: Father of Saul, Benjamite (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Saul's servant
characters.note: Servant who accompanies Saul seeking donkeys (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Saul's uncle
characters.note: Uncle who questions Saul after Samuel's anointing (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Nahash the Ammonite
characters.note: King of the Ammonites besieging Jabesh Gilead (1 Samuel).

characters.name: the men of Jabesh
characters.note: Inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Jonathan
characters.note: Son of Saul, friend of David (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Jonathan's armor bearer
aliases: the young man who bore his armor
characters.note: Young man who fights beside Jonathan; unnamed (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Ahijah
characters.note: Priest wearing the ephod with Saul (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Agag
characters.note: King of the Amalekites spared by Saul and killed by Samuel (1 Samuel).

characters.name: the Amalekites
characters.note: People struck by Saul (1 Samuel); also the raiders of Ziklag. The same people as in Exodus.

characters.name: the Kenites
characters.note: People spared by Saul (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Jesse
characters.note: Father of David and seven or eight sons (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Eliab
characters.note: Eldest son of Jesse, David's brother (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Shammah
characters.note: Son of Jesse, David's brother (1 Samuel).

characters.name: David
characters.note: Shepherd anointed as king; later outlaw and king (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Goliath
characters.note: Philistine champion of Gath slain by David (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Goliath's shield bearer
aliases: the man who bore the shield
characters.note: Attendant of Goliath (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Merab
characters.note: Elder daughter of Saul (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Michal
characters.note: Younger daughter of Saul, loves David, wife of David (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Abner
characters.note: Son of Ner, commander of Saul's army and Saul's cousin (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Adriel the Meholathite
characters.note: Husband of Merab (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Doeg the Edomite
characters.note: Servant of Saul who informs on and slays the priests (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Ahimelech
characters.note: Priest of Nob, son of Ahitub (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Abiathar
characters.note: Priest, son of Ahimelech, escapes to David (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Achish
characters.note: Philistine king of Gath who gives David Ziklag (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Gad
characters.note: Prophet who advises David (1 Samuel).

characters.name: the Ziphites
characters.note: Men of Ziph who betray David (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Nabal
characters.note: Rich, surly man of Carmel, husband of Abigail (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Abigail
characters.note: Intelligent wife of Nabal, later wife of David (1 Samuel).

characters.name: a young man of Nabal's
characters.note: Servant who warns Abigail (1 Samuel).

characters.name: David's young men
aliases: the young men who follow David
characters.note: Messengers sent to Nabal (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Palti
characters.note: Husband of Michal before David (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Abishai
characters.note: Nephew of David, accompanies him into Saul's camp (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Ahinoam
characters.note: Wife of David from Jezreel (1 Samuel).

characters.name: an Egyptian youth
characters.note: Servant of an Amalekite who guides David (1 Samuel).

characters.name: the archers
characters.note: Philistine archers who wound Saul (1 Samuel).

characters.name: the woman with a familiar spirit
characters.note: Medium at Endor who calls up Samuel (1 Samuel).

characters.name: Jesus
characters.note: Central figure; the Word made flesh who teaches, heals, is crucified and raised (John).

characters.name: John the Baptist
characters.note: Man sent from God who baptizes and testifies to the light; distinct from John the apostle (John).

characters.name: Andrew
characters.note: Disciple, Simon Peter's brother, from Bethsaida (John).

characters.name: Simon Peter
characters.note: Disciple renamed Cephas (Peter) by Jesus (John).

characters.name: Philip
characters.note: Disciple from Bethsaida who brings Nathanael to Jesus (John).

characters.name: Nathanael
characters.note: Man from Cana who becomes a disciple (John).

characters.name: Mary, mother of Jesus
characters.note: Mother of Jesus at the wedding in Cana and at the cross (John). Not the same as Mary Magdalene or Mary of Bethany.

characters.name: Mary Magdalene
characters.note: Woman who sees the risen Jesus at the tomb (John).

characters.name: Mary of Bethany
characters.note: Sister of Martha and Lazarus who anoints Jesus (John).

characters.name: Martha
characters.note: Sister of Mary and Lazarus of Bethany (John).

characters.name: Lazarus
characters.note: Man from Bethany raised from the dead by Jesus (John).

characters.name: Nicodemus
characters.note: Pharisee and ruler who comes to Jesus by night (John).

characters.name: the Samaritan woman
characters.note: Woman of Sychar who talks with Jesus at Jacob's well (John).

characters.name: the nobleman
characters.note: Official whose son is healed at Capernaum (John).

characters.name: the sick man
aliases: the man who had been sick thirty-eight years
characters.note: Man healed at the pool of Bethesda (John).

characters.name: the man born blind
characters.note: Man born blind whom Jesus heals with mud at Siloam (John).

characters.name: Thomas
characters.note: Disciple who doubts the resurrection until he sees Jesus (John).

characters.name: Judas Iscariot
characters.note: Disciple who betrays Jesus; not to be confused with Judas, not Iscariot (John).

characters.name: Judas (not Iscariot)
characters.note: Disciple who asks Jesus why he will reveal himself only to his disciples (John).

characters.name: Pilate
characters.note: Roman governor who examines Jesus and has him crucified (John).

characters.name: Caiaphas
characters.note: High priest who counsels that one man should die for the people (John).

characters.name: Annas
characters.note: Father-in-law of Caiaphas who questions Jesus first (John).

characters.name: Barabbas
characters.note: Robber released instead of Jesus (John).

characters.name: Joseph of Arimathaea
characters.note: Disciple who asks Pilate for Jesus' body (John). Not the same as Joseph son of Jacob in Exodus.

characters.name: Malchus
characters.note: Servant whose ear Peter cuts off (John).

characters.name: the maid who kept the door
characters.note: Servant woman who asks Peter if he is a disciple (John).

characters.name: the two angels
characters.note: Angels sitting in the tomb; shown as figures in white (John).

characters.name: the disciple whom Jesus loved
characters.note: Unnamed disciple at the supper, at the cross and at the empty tomb (John).

characters.name: the soldiers
characters.note: Roman soldiers and temple officers who arrest, mock and crucify Jesus (John).

characters.name: the Pharisees
characters.note: Religious leaders who oppose Jesus (John).

characters.name: the Jews
characters.note: Jewish leaders and crowds who debate and oppose Jesus in the Gospel's usage (John).

characters.name: the disciples
characters.note: Jesus' followers acting together (John).

characters.name: Satan
characters.note: Adversary who enters Judas; not shown as a human (John).

locations.name: Maon

brief.era: Spans several periods: Bronze Age Egypt and the Sinai wilderness (Exodus, c. 13th century BCE); the transition from judges to monarchy in Israel (1 Samuel, c. 11th century BCE); and first-century Roman Judea and Galilee (John). Illustrators should favor an ancient Near Eastern look for each section rather than a single date.
brief.place: Egypt (palace, Nile, Goshen, brick fields), Midian, Sinai and the Red Sea; the hill country and Philistine cities (Shiloh, Ramah, Gibeah, Bethlehem, the valley of Elah, Ashdod, Gath, Ekron); Galilee, Samaria and Jerusalem with lakeside, village, well, pool, temple and garden settings.
brief.dress: Egyptians in linen kilts and wigs, Pharaoh in royal headdress; Israelites in simple tunics and cloaks; priests in linen tunics, sashes, turbans and the ephod and breastplate of Exodus; shepherds and David with staff, sling and bag; Saul and kings in finer robes; Philistines in bronze helmets, mail and shin armor; first-century Jews in tunics, outer cloaks and sandals; Roman soldiers and Pilate in military or governor's dress; Jesus in plain garments.
brief.buildings_and_objects: Brick storage cities, the papyrus basket, the burning bush, the tabernacle with curtains, boards, veil, ark with cherubim, lampstand and altars; Shiloh sanctuary and the ark carried on poles or drawn by a cart; mud-brick houses, cave strongholds, threshing floors; stone water pots, nets and boats, Jacob's well, pools with porches, a rock-cut tomb with linen cloths, a cross and crown of thorns; stone tablets; the pillar of cloud and fire.
depiction_rules: Never depict God or Yahweh as a human figure; show God through fire, cloud, light, wind, thunder, a voice, or an angel as radiance without a fixed face.
Show the Holy Spirit as a dove only where the text describes it, at the baptism of Jesus.
Depict Satan and the devil as unseen or a shadowy presence; show evil spirits through their effect on people (e.g., Saul).
Depict Dagon's fallen idol in Ashdod headless and handless, not as a complete statue.
Show angels in white as human-like figures seated in the tomb, not winged beings.
Show Samuel's ghost at Endor as an old man in a robe rising from the ground, not a vivid apparition.
The ark is a gold-covered chest, not a humanoid or monstrous figure.
Tabernacle furnishings must match the patterns in Exodus 25-27 and 35-40.
Pharaoh and the Egyptians are oppressors but not caricatures; Jewish leaders and crowds in John are not caricatured either, the conflict being with specific authorities.
Plagues appear as escalating natural disasters with Israelites spared in Goshen.
Moses may show a radiant face after Sinai and wear a veil; the risen Jesus has no special glow unless the text calls for it.
Goliath is huge and armored, not comic; David is a young, ruddy shepherd youth.
Keep named individuals distinct (e.g., Mary Magdalene, Mary of Bethany, Mary the mother of Jesus) rather than generic crowds.
